Trigger-4 lane is actively moving; no duplicate implementation is authorized from this delta

finding: The current F2 completion epistemics correctly separates target positive readback from counterevidence, and WP-1202 correctly treats systemd-user reachability as a runtime check. The missing discriminating layer is provenance-rich lifecycle evidence: systemd can give manager-observed service lifecycle/invocation evidence, but none of READY=1, active/running, Result=success or systemctl start success is equivalent to external target-function readback.
recommended_delta: Add or reuse one generic typed TargetRuntimeLifecycleWitness abstraction, with systemd-user as its first producer adapter. Bind the witness to target profile generation/digest, target id, UID/manager scope, unit identity, InvocationID and observed manager state. CompletionGate may use it to satisfy lifecycle/process obligations, but a separate externally observed function-readback witness remains mandatory for REAL_READBACK_VERIFIED and all higher target completion. After restart/relogin/reboot, stale lifecycle/readback evidence is invalid until a new InvocationID and fresh function readback are observed.
why_not_a_systemd_specific_truth_layer: A systemd-only canonical layer would overfit one init/service manager and duplicate authority. The durable architecture rule is generic lifecycle-evidence provenance; systemd is an adapter/probe implementation on Ubuntu.
